text.p: Dutch electronics firm Philips on Monday declined to comment on a newspaper report that it could post a 1996 loss by booking the costs of severing ties with its troubled German unit Grundig.
"We disclose our 1996 figures on February 13 and we do not anticipate anything until that date," a Philips spokesman said.
On Saturday newspaper De Volkskrant said the restructuring Philips had already set aside under management board chairman Cor Boonstra would not cover the cost of shedding its interests in Grundig.
"He needs another 700 million guilders to throw the German subsidiary out of the house," De Volkskrant said.

In 1995 the company posted a 30 percent rise in net income from normal operations to 2.68 billion guilders. In the first nine months of 1996, net income from normal operations dwindled to 804 million from a year-earlier 1.67 billion.
The company said then it would take a charge of approximately one billion guilders before tax in the fourth quarter.
